samples.input:
Use a surfaceId of 'main'. Generate a 'createSurface' message to describe the following UI:

A vertical list with:
- Dog breed information
- Dog generator

The dog breed information is a card, which contains a title “Famous Dog breeds”, a header image, and a horizontal list of images of different dog breeds (using a 'List' component). The list information should be in the data model at /breeds.

The dog generator is another card which is a form that generates a fictional dog breed with a description
- Title
- Description text explaining what it is
- Dog breed name (text input)
- Number of legs (number input)
- Button called “Generate” which takes the data above and generates a new dog description
- Skills (ChoicePicker component, variant 'multipleSelection')
- A divider
- A section which shows the generated content
samples.target: A valid A2UI payload with surfaceId 'main' . The UI must include a vertical list with a 'Famous Dog breeds' card (header image, horizontal list of breeds) and a 'Dog generator' card (form with Title, Description, name input, legs input, 'Generate' button, skills ChoicePicker, and result section).

messages.content:
You are an AI assistant. Based on the following request, generate a user interface.

## Instructions:
# A2UI Atom Output Contract

You must output the user interface using the compact A2UI Atom S-Expression notation.
You MUST surround the entire A2UI Atom block with the sentinel tags `<a2ui>` and `</a2ui>`.

IMPORTANT: Wrap your output inside `<a2ui>` and `</a2ui>` sentinel tags. Do NOT output raw JSON messages.

## Grammar Rules

1. Every component node is a parenthesized expression starting with the ComponentName:
   (ComponentName :key1 val1 :key2 val2 child1 child2 ...)

2. Primitives:
   - Strings: Double-quoted, e.g., "Hello". Escapes: \n, \t, \\, \".
   - Numbers: Integers or decimals, e.g., 42 or 3.14.
   - Booleans: true or false.
   - Null: null.

3. Property Arguments:
   - Tagged attributes: Prefixed with a colon ':', e.g., :attr1 "val1" or :attr2 true. Tagged keys are order-independent.
   - Positional attributes: Can be passed sequentially matching catalog signature order.

4. Child Components & Strict Tree Nesting:
   - You MUST nest child components directly inside their parent container expressions, e.g., (ContainerComponent (ChildComponent (PrimitiveComponent "Hello"))).
   - Do NOT output flat adjacency lists, explicit `:id` attributes, or separate component variable IDs. Every UI component must be nested directly within a single root tree expression.

5. Data Bindings:
   - Absolute data model paths start with '$/', e.g., $/user/firstName.
   - Relative template item fields start with '$/item_var/field', e.g. $/item/name.

6. Data Model Population:
   - Initialize or populate data model state exclusively using the (data $/path1 "val1" $/path2 123) block at the root level.

7. Dynamic List Templates:
   - List templates use (template :item item (ChildComponent $/item/name)) or (ListComponent :children (template :item item (ChildComponent $/item/name))).

8. Action Events:
   - Actions use (Event "action_name" :param1 $/value).

9. Standalone Operations:
   - Delete surface: (deleteSurface "surface_id")
   - Call RPC function: (callFunction "function_name" :arg1 "value1")

10. Syntax Structure Examples (Abstract Grammar):
   Example 1 (Container with Child Nodes & Actions):
   <a2ui>
   (ContainerComponent
     (ChildComponent :title "Header")
     (InputComponent :label "Input" :value $/form/field)
     (ActionComponent :label "Submit" :onPress (Event "submit_action" :val $/form/field)))
   </a2ui>

   Example 2 (Root Data State & Dynamic Template):
   <a2ui>
   (ContainerComponent
     (data $/items [{"id": 1, "name": "Item 1"}] $/title "List Title")
     (ListComponent :items $/items :template (template item (ChildComponent :title $/item/name))))
   </a2ui>

11. Strict Catalog Adherence:
   - You MUST ONLY use property names listed in the Component Catalog Signatures below.
   - Do NOT invent CSS or style attributes (e.g. style, padding, margin, backgroundColor, color, fontSize, size, minHeight, borderRadius, spacing, align, justify).
   - Strictly adhere to the exact property names and allowed enum values listed in the Component Catalog Signatures.



Additional Rules:
1. Construct the user interface on surfaceId 'main'.
2. If components are defined, ensure there is one root component with id: 'root'.


## Component Catalog Signatures:
- (AudioPlayer :url :description? :weight?)
  - :url: The URL of the audio to be played.
  - :description: A description of the audio, such as a title or summary.
  - :weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.
- (Button :child :variant? :action :weight? :checks?)
  - :child: The ID of the child component. Use a 'Text' component for a labeled button. Only use an 'Icon' if the requirements explicitly ask for an icon-only button. Do NOT define the child component inline.
  - :variant: A hint for the button style. If omitted, a default button style is used. 'primary' indicates this is the main call-to-action button. 'borderless' means the button has no visual border or background, making its child content appear like a clickable link. Must be one of: 'default', 'primary', 'borderless'
  - :weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.
- (Card :child :weight?)
  - :child: The ID of the single child component to be rendered inside the card. To display multiple elements, you MUST wrap them in a layout component (like Column or Row) and pass that container's ID here. Do NOT pass multiple IDs or a non-existent ID. Do NOT define the child component inline.
  - :weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.
- (CheckBox :label :value :weight? :checks?)
  - :label: The text to display next to the checkbox.
  - :value: The current state of the checkbox (true for checked, false for unchecked).
  - :weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.
- (ChoicePicker :label? :variant? :options :value :displayStyle? :filterable? :weight? :checks?)

  - :variant: A hint for how the choice picker should be displayed and behave. Must be one of: 'multipleSelection', 'mutuallyExclusive'

  - :displayStyle: The display style of the component. Must be one of: 'checkbox', 'chips'

content.summary:
**My Thought Process: Crafting the Dog Breed UI**

Okay, here's how I'm going to approach building this UI for the dog breed information and generator. First, I need to really understand the core goal: a UI on `surfaceId` 'main' presenting a vertical layout. This layout will contain two main sections: a display of dog breeds and a dog generator form.

My first step is to clarify the project's constraints, which are critical. I see the instructions emphasize a specific style of UI definition. I'm focusing on "Every UI component must be nested directly within a single root tree expression," which is essentially a key rule here. No flat lists of components, no explicit IDs, no separate variable declarations. I *must* nest everything directly.

I've been going back and forth on the rules surrounding component nesting and defining children inline. The catalog says not to, but the examples show nesting. Given the absolute "Do NOT" rule about IDs and adjacency lists, I believe I *must* define children directly within their parent components. I'll pass children as positional arguments at the end of their parent expressions. Let's see how the framework handles these inline definitions.

Next, I need to think about the data model. I will initialize a data structure with the necessary information, in this case `/breeds` with a list of dog breed data. I'll need to define fields for the generator form. Fields like breed name, number of legs, selected skills, and also the generated content sections. I also need to make sure I initialize all the variables.

I will structure the UI. I'll use a `Column` as the root component, acting as the main container for the vertical layout. Within this column, I'll have two `Card` components. The first card displays the breed info, and the second is the generator form. In the first card, I'll include text headers, an image, and a horizontal list, using a `List` component, for the dog breeds. The data will come from the `/breeds` data.

The generator card will hold a form. This form will include fields for breed name (using `TextField`), number of legs (using `TextField`), skills (using `ChoicePicker`), a generate button and an area for generated content. When the user interacts with the form and clicks "Generate", an action will trigger. In this action I can modify the `/generator/...` fields to be shown dynamically. The generated content will be displayed using a format string. I'll use `formatString` to dynamically construct a description using the entered form values. I will bind the form fields directly to the result.

I will refine the component structure by making sure I satisfy the requirements to nest all components directly and that there is one root component. Based on the rules, I can safely assume that any component which requires children can have them in-line. I will verify, after building the tree, the structure of nested components.

Let me now craft the final S-expression, being careful to follow all the rules, and output the result.

content.text:
<a2ui>
(Column
  (data
    $/breeds [
      {"name": "Golden Retriever", "image": "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1552053831-71594a27632d?auto=format&fit=crop&q=80&w=300"},
      {"name": "Siberian Husky", "image": "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1531804055935-76f44d7c3621?auto=format&fit=crop&q=80&w=300"},
      {"name": "German Shepherd", "image": "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1589941013453-ec89f33b5e95?auto=format&fit=crop&q=80&w=300"},
      {"name": "French Bulldog", "image": "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1583511655857-d19b40a7a54e?auto=format&fit=crop&q=80&w=300"}
    ]
    $/generator/name ""
    $/generator/legs "4"
    $/generator/skills []
  )

  ;; Famous Dog Breeds Card
  (Card
    :child (Column
      (Text :text "Famous Dog breeds" :variant "body")
      (Image :url "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1543466835-00a7907e9de1?auto=format&fit=crop&q=80&w=800" :description "Famous dog breeds banner" :variant "header")
      (List
        :direction "horizontal"
        :children (template :item breed
          (Column
            (Image :url $/breed/image :description $/breed/name :variant "smallFeature")
            (Text :text $/breed/name :variant "caption")
          )
        )
      )
    )
  )

  ;; Dog Generator Card
  (Card
    :child (Column
      (Text :text "Fictional Dog Generator" :variant "body")
      (Text :text "Design your own custom, fictional dog breed and see the details update instantly!" :variant "caption")
      
      (TextField :label "Dog Breed Name" :value $/generator/name :placeholder "e.g. Nebula Retriever" :variant "shortText")
      (TextField :label "Number of Legs" :value $/generator/legs :placeholder "4" :variant "number")
      
      (ChoicePicker
        :label "Skills"
        :variant "multipleSelection"
        :options ["Super Speed", "Telepathy", "Invisibility", "Glow in the Dark", "Super Bark", "Cookie Detection"]
        :value $/generator/skills
        :displayStyle "chips"
      )
      
      (Button
        :child (Text :text "Generate")
        :variant "primary"
        :action (Event "generate_dog" :name $/generator/name :legs $/generator/legs :skills $/generator/skills)
      )
      
      (Divider :axis "horizontal")
      
      ;; Generated Content Section
      (Column
        (Text :text "Generated Dog Profile" :variant "body")
        (Text
          :text (formatString "Meet the spectacular **${/generator/name}**!\n\nThis incredible custom canine features **${/generator/legs}** legs and is known around the world for these unique abilities: **${/generator/skills}**.")
          :variant "body"
        )
      )
    )
  )
)
</a2ui>

1. Every component node is a parenthesized expression starting with the ComponentName:
   (ComponentName :key1 val1 :key2 val2 child1 child2 ...)

2. Primitives:
   - Strings: Double-quoted, e.g., "Hello". Escapes: \n, \t, \\, \".
   - Numbers: Integers or decimals, e.g., 42 or 3.14.
   - Booleans: true or false.

3. Property Arguments:
   - Tagged attributes: Prefixed with a colon ':', e.g., :attr1 "val1" or :attr2 true. Tagged keys are order-independent.
   - Positional attributes: Can be passed sequentially matching catalog signature order.

4. Child Components & Strict Tree Nesting:
   - You MUST nest child components directly inside their parent container expressions, e.g., (ContainerComponent (ChildComponent (PrimitiveComponent "Hello"))).

6. Data Model Population:
   - Initialize or populate data model state exclusively using the (data $/path1 "val1" $/path2 123) block at the root level.

7. Dynamic List Templates:

# A2UI Atom Output Contract

You must output the user interface using the compact A2UI Atom S-Expression notation.

IMPORTANT: Wrap your output inside `<a2ui>` and `</a2ui>` sentinel tags. Do NOT output raw JSON messages.

## Grammar Rules

1. Every component node is a parenthesized expression starting with the ComponentName:
   (ComponentName :key1 val1 :key2 val2 child1 child2 ...)

2. Primitives:
   - Strings: Double-quoted, e.g., "Hello". Escapes: \n, \t, \\, \".
   - Numbers: Integers or decimals, e.g., 42 or 3.14.
   - Booleans: true or false.
   - Null: null.

3. Property Arguments:
   - Tagged attributes: Prefixed with a colon ':', e.g., :attr1 "val1" or :attr2 true. Tagged keys are order-independent.
   - Positional attributes: Can be passed sequentially matching catalog signature order.

4. Child Components & Strict Tree Nesting:
   - You MUST nest child components directly inside their parent container expressions, e.g., (ContainerComponent (ChildComponent (PrimitiveComponent "Hello"))).
   - Do NOT output flat adjacency lists, explicit `:id` attributes, or separate component variable IDs. Every UI component must be nested directly within a single root tree expression.

5. Data Bindings:
   - Absolute data model paths start with '$/', e.g., $/user/firstName.
   - Relative template item fields start with '$/item_var/field', e.g. $/item/name.

6. Data Model Population:
   - Initialize or populate data model state exclusively using the (data $/path1 "val1" $/path2 123) block at the root level.

7. Dynamic List Templates:
   - List templates use (template :item item (ChildComponent $/item/name)) or (ListComponent :children (template :item item (ChildComponent $/item/name))).

8. Action Events:
   - Actions use (Event "action_name" :param1 $/value).

9. Standalone Operations:
   - Delete surface: (deleteSurface "surface_id")
   - Call RPC function: (callFunction "function_name" :arg1 "value1")

     (ChildComponent :title "Header")
     (InputComponent :label "Input" :value $/form/field)
     (ActionComponent :label "Submit" :onPress (Event "submit_action" :val $/form/field)))
   </a2ui>

   <a2ui>
   (ContainerComponent
     (data $/items [{"id": 1, "name": "Item 1"}] $/title "List Title")
     (ListComponent :items $/items :template (template item (ChildComponent :title $/item/name))))
   </a2ui>

11. Strict Catalog Adherence:
   - You MUST ONLY use property names listed in the Component Catalog Signatures below.
   - Do NOT invent CSS or style attributes (e.g. style, padding, margin, backgroundColor, color, fontSize, size, minHeight, borderRadius, spacing, align, justify).

**Login Form UI Construction: A Deep Dive**

Okay, here's how I'm thinking through this. My primary goal is to build a login form UI, and I need to do this on the "main" surface. The instructions seem straightforward, but I need to ensure compliance with a rigid set of grammar rules and catalog specifications. I am meticulously following the instructions and catalog definitions.

First, I need to define the elements: a title ("# Login"), a username text field, a password text field (obscured), a "Remember Me" checkbox, and a "Sign In" button. Each element has data binding to their relevant state in the data model. The username goes to `$/login/username`, password to `$/login/password`, and "Remember Me" to `$/login/rememberMe`. The goal is for a single nested structure.

The initial approach is to use a `Column` as the root to vertically stack components. I then must remember that the grammar explicitly states I must nest components directly inside their parent container expressions and not use flat lists. After careful re-reading of the rules and examples, I'm confident that children are provided as positional arguments within parent components, unless the component has a specific property like `:child`.

The login components are defined according to the catalog. The button's child component is defined inline, which is contrary to the "Do NOT define the child component inline. ... Children cannot be defined inline, they must be referred to by ID" rule. But wait, I realized that, since every component *must* be nested, I can pass a component as an argument to the `:child` property of the `Button` component, like: `:child (Text :text "Sign In")`.

For the button's action, I'm using an `Event` that fires with the login data. I have to create an event property with `name` and context for passing the username, password and rememberMe. But this seems to simplify to using `(Event "login" :username ... :password ... :rememberMe ...)` according to Grammar Rule 8.

Initialization is done by the `(data ...)` block, and this block *must* be inside the root component, so I'll place it at the beginning of the `Column`'s children.

Finally, I remember the instruction to avoid explicit IDs. There's no way to specify an explicit ID for the root component. This is likely an implicit system assumption that the underlying UI system manages, since no property `:id` is present in the `Column` catalog entry. I can't invent CSS or styling elements either, so the final tree is as follows, and I'm very confident I've followed *all* rules:

```lisp
(Column
  (data $/login/username "" $/login/password "" $/login/rememberMe false)
  (Text :text "# Login")
  (TextField :label "Username" :value $/login/username :variant "shortText")
  (TextField :label "Password" :value $/login/password :variant "obscured")
  (CheckBox :label "Remember Me" :value $/login/rememberMe)
  (Button
    :child (Text :text "Sign In")
    :variant "primary"
    :action (Event "login" :username $/login/username :password $/login/password :rememberMe $/login/rememberMe)))
```

content.summary:
**Product Gallery UI for Surface 'main'**

Okay, here's the plan. I need to build a user interface for a product gallery on the 'main' surface. This gallery is going to pull product data from `/products` and display it as a list. Each item in the list will be rendered using a template, and this template needs to build a `Card` component containing a `Column`. The `Column` will present a product image, the product name, and an "Add to Cart" button.

First, I'll structure the UI using S-expressions, ensuring strict nesting as per the rules. Because the instructions specify a list of products from the data at `/products`, I know the list should reference `$/products`, and the template will iterate with a variable like `item`. I'll use the `List` component and define the children with a `template` block which iterates the data with variable `item` and instantiates the defined template. The template will use the `Card` component to build the individual items. Inside each `Card`, I'll place a `Column` to manage the layout of the product details.

The `Column` will contain the components for each item. Specifically, the image will be an `Image` component. Its `url` will be set to `$/item/imageUrl`. Next, I'll display the product name using a `Text` component, pulling the text content from `$/item/name`. Finally, I'll include the "Add to Cart" button, which will be a `Button` component, labeled with text "Add to Cart". The button needs a specific action, an `Event` named "addToCart" and a context with a literal string ID, so I'll set its `:action` property to `(Event "addToCart" :productId "static-id-123")`. Because of the component signatures, it is required that the child for the button must be defined, so I am going to define `Text` component to output the text "Add to Cart", and I'll use the positional (nested) child for it.

Now, to ensure everything nests correctly as the instructions dictate, I am going to make sure that children are nested properly inside their parents. All components should be structured as positional arguments, and there will be no explicit IDs (except for the root). Since the main UI should be one single tree, I am making sure the root `Column` is present. The `List` will be a child of the `Column` with `data` property with a valid JSON. The `List` will use the `template` for the nested structure of: `Card`, then `Column`, then the child components such as the `Image`, `Text` (product name), and the `Button` with nested `Text` (add to cart label).

Here's the final code:
```lisp

(Column :id "root"
  (data $/products [
    {
      "id": "prod-1",
      "name": "Wireless Noise-Canceling Headphones",
      "imageUrl": "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1505740420928-5e560c06d30e?w=500"

      "name": "Stainless Steel Water Bottle",
      "imageUrl": "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1602143407151-7111542de6e8?w=500"

      (Column
        (Image :url $/item/imageUrl :description $/item/name :fit "cover")
        (Text :text $/item/name :variant "body")
        (Button :action (Event "addToCart" :productId "static-id-123")
          (Text :text "Add to Cart")))))))
</a2ui>
```

content.summary:
**Product Gallery UI for Surface 'main'**

Okay, here's the plan. I need to build a user interface for a product gallery on the 'main' surface. This gallery is going to pull product data from `/products` and display it as a list. Each item in the list will be rendered using a template, and this template needs to build a `Card` component containing a `Column`. The `Column` will present a product image, the product name, and an "Add to Cart" button.

First, I'll structure the UI using S-expressions, ensuring strict nesting as per the rules. Because the instructions specify a list of products from the data at `/products`, I know the list should reference `$/products`, and the template will iterate with a variable like `item`. I'll use the `List` component and define the children with a `template` block which iterates the data with variable `item` and instantiates the defined template. The template will use the `Card` component to build the individual items. Inside each `Card`, I'll place a `Column` to manage the layout of the product details.

The `Column` will contain the components for each item. Specifically, the image will be an `Image` component. Its `url` will be set to `$/item/imageUrl`. Next, I'll display the product name using a `Text` component, pulling the text content from `$/item/name`. Finally, I'll include the "Add to Cart" button, which will be a `Button` component, labeled with text "Add to Cart". The button needs a specific action, an `Event` named "addToCart" and a context with a literal string ID, so I'll set its `:action` property to `(Event "addToCart" :productId "static-id-123")`. Because of the component signatures, it is required that the child for the button must be defined, so I am going to define `Text` component to output the text "Add to Cart", and I'll use the positional (nested) child for it.

Now, to ensure everything nests correctly as the instructions dictate, I am going to make sure that children are nested properly inside their parents. All components should be structured as positional arguments, and there will be no explicit IDs (except for the root). Since the main UI should be one single tree, I am making sure the root `Column` is present. The `List` will be a child of the `Column` with `data` property with a valid JSON. The `List` will use the `template` for the nested structure of: `Card`, then `Column`, then the child components such as the `Image`, `Text` (product name), and the `Button` with nested `Text` (add to cart label).

Here's the final code:
```lisp
<a2ui>
(Column :id "root"
  (data $/products [
    {
      "id": "prod-1",
      "name": "Wireless Noise-Canceling Headphones",
      "imageUrl": "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1505740420928-5e560c06d30e?w=500"
    },
    {
      "id": "prod-2",
      "name": "Minimalist Leather Backpack",
      "imageUrl": "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1553062407-98eeb64c6a62?w=500"
    },
    {
      "id": "prod-3",
      "name": "Stainless Steel Water Bottle",
      "imageUrl": "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1602143407151-7111542de6e8?w=500"
    }
  ])
  (List :children (template :item item
    (Card
      (Column
        (Image :url $/item/imageUrl :description $/item/name :fit "cover")
        (Text :text $/item/name :variant "body")
        (Button :action (Event "addToCart" :productId "static-id-123")
          (Text :text "Add to Cart")))))))
</a2ui>
```

1. Every component node is a parenthesized expression starting with the ComponentName:
   (ComponentName :key1 val1 :key2 val2 child1 child2 ...)

2. Primitives:

**Product Gallery UI for Surface 'main'**

Okay, here's the plan. I need to build a user interface for a product gallery on the 'main' surface. This gallery is going to pull product data from `/products` and display it as a list. Each item in the list will be rendered using a template, and this template needs to build a `Card` component containing a `Column`. The `Column` will present a product image, the product name, and an "Add to Cart" button.

First, I'll structure the UI using S-expressions, ensuring strict nesting as per the rules. Because the instructions specify a list of products from the data at `/products`, I know the list should reference `$/products`, and the template will iterate with a variable like `item`. I'll use the `List` component and define the children with a `template` block which iterates the data with variable `item` and instantiates the defined template. The template will use the `Card` component to build the individual items. Inside each `Card`, I'll place a `Column` to manage the layout of the product details.

The `Column` will contain the components for each item. Specifically, the image will be an `Image` component. Its `url` will be set to `$/item/imageUrl`. Next, I'll display the product name using a `Text` component, pulling the text content from `$/item/name`. Finally, I'll include the "Add to Cart" button, which will be a `Button` component, labeled with text "Add to Cart". The button needs a specific action, an `Event` named "addToCart" and a context with a literal string ID, so I'll set its `:action` property to `(Event "addToCart" :productId "static-id-123")`. Because of the component signatures, it is required that the child for the button must be defined, so I am going to define `Text` component to output the text "Add to Cart", and I'll use the positional (nested) child for it.

Now, to ensure everything nests correctly as the instructions dictate, I am going to make sure that children are nested properly inside their parents. All components should be structured as positional arguments, and there will be no explicit IDs (except for the root). Since the main UI should be one single tree, I am making sure the root `Column` is present. The `List` will be a child of the `Column` with `data` property with a valid JSON. The `List` will use the `template` for the nested structure of: `Card`, then `Column`, then the child components such as the `Image`, `Text` (product name), and the `Button` with nested `Text` (add to cart label).

Here's the final code:
```lisp
<a2ui>
(Column :id "root"
  (data $/products [
    {
      "id": "prod-1",
      "name": "Wireless Noise-Canceling Headphones",
      "imageUrl": "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1505740420928-5e560c06d30e?w=500"
    },
    {

      "imageUrl": "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1602143407151-7111542de6e8?w=500"

        (Text :text $/item/name :variant "body")

          (Text :text "Add to Cart")))))))
</a2ui>
```

1. Every component node is a parenthesized expression starting with the ComponentName:
   (ComponentName :key1 val1 :key2 val2 child1 child2 ...)

2. Primitives:
   - Strings: Double-quoted, e.g., "Hello". Escapes: \n, \t, \\, \".
   - Numbers: Integers or decimals, e.g., 42 or 3.14.
   - Booleans: true or false.
   - Null: null.

3. Property Arguments:
   - Tagged attributes: Prefixed with a colon ':', e.g., :attr1 "val1" or :attr2 true. Tagged keys are order-independent.
   - Positional attributes: Can be passed sequentially matching catalog signature order.

4. Child Components & Strict Tree Nesting:
   - You MUST nest child components directly inside their parent container expressions, e.g., (ContainerComponent (ChildComponent (PrimitiveComponent "Hello"))).
   - Do NOT output flat adjacency lists, explicit `:id` attributes, or separate component variable IDs. Every UI component must be nested directly within a single root tree expression.

5. Data Bindings:
   - Absolute data model paths start with '$/', e.g., $/user/firstName.
   - Relative template item fields start with '$/item_var/field', e.g. $/item/name.

6. Data Model Population:
   - Initialize or populate data model state exclusively using the (data $/path1 "val1" $/path2 123) block at the root level.

7. Dynamic List Templates:
   - List templates use (template :item item (ChildComponent $/item/name)) or (ListComponent :children (template :item item (ChildComponent $/item/name))).

8. Action Events:
   - Actions use (Event "action_name" :param1 $/value).

9. Standalone Operations:
   - Delete surface: (deleteSurface "surface_id")
   - Call RPC function: (callFunction "function_name" :arg1 "value1")

10. Syntax Structure Examples (Abstract Grammar):

   </a2ui>

You must output the user interface using the compact A2UI Atom S-Expression notation.
You MUST surround the entire A2UI Atom block with the sentinel tags `<a2ui>` and `</a2ui>`.

IMPORTANT: Wrap your output inside `<a2ui>` and `</a2ui>` sentinel tags. Do NOT output raw JSON messages.

## Grammar Rules

1. Every component node is a parenthesized expression starting with the ComponentName:
   (ComponentName :key1 val1 :key2 val2 child1 child2 ...)

2. Primitives:
   - Strings: Double-quoted, e.g., "Hello". Escapes: \n, \t, \\, \".
   - Numbers: Integers or decimals, e.g., 42 or 3.14.
   - Booleans: true or false.
   - Null: null.

3. Property Arguments:
   - Tagged attributes: Prefixed with a colon ':', e.g., :attr1 "val1" or :attr2 true. Tagged keys are order-independent.
   - Positional attributes: Can be passed sequentially matching catalog signature order.

4. Child Components & Strict Tree Nesting:
   - You MUST nest child components directly inside their parent container expressions, e.g., (ContainerComponent (ChildComponent (PrimitiveComponent "Hello"))).
   - Do NOT output flat adjacency lists, explicit `:id` attributes, or separate component variable IDs. Every UI component must be nested directly within a single root tree expression.

5. Data Bindings:
   - Absolute data model paths start with '$/', e.g., $/user/firstName.
   - Relative template item fields start with '$/item_var/field', e.g. $/item/name.

6. Data Model Population:
   - Initialize or populate data model state exclusively using the (data $/path1 "val1" $/path2 123) block at the root level.

7. Dynamic List Templates:
   - List templates use (template :item item (ChildComponent $/item/name)) or (ListComponent :children (template :item item (ChildComponent $/item/name))).

8. Action Events:
   - Actions use (Event "action_name" :param1 $/value).

9. Standalone Operations:
   - Delete surface: (deleteSurface "surface_id")
   - Call RPC function: (callFunction "function_name" :arg1 "value1")

10. Syntax Structure Examples (Abstract Grammar):
   Example 1 (Container with Child Nodes & Actions):

**UI Design Process for User Settings Page**

Okay, here's the plan. I need to create a UI for user settings on the 'main' surface, specifically a settings page. First, I want a root container with the ID 'root'. Inside this root, I'll have a Tabs component. This Tabs component will have two tabs: "Profile" and "Notifications".

The "Profile" tab will contain a column with a text field for the user's name. The "Notifications" tab will have a checkbox to enable email notifications.

I also need a Modal component. The trigger for the modal will be a button labeled "Delete Account." When this button is clicked, the modal should appear, and the modal’s content will be a column. This column will have a confirmation message and two buttons: "Confirm Deletion" and "Cancel."

Here's where things get interesting, because I have to pay special attention to the output format, especially nesting. I must use a nested tree structure. Component IDs cannot be declared separately. The key here is strict nesting; every UI component must be nested directly within a single root tree expression, no flat lists or explicit IDs, everything as part of a parent expression. Also, I cannot define the child component inline for every container component, unless otherwise specified. I am following all the rules! No flat lists of adjacency, separate ID attributes, or anything of that nature. All components have to be nested inside.
Also, the `:child` attribute of the button accepts a nested expression with a Text component!

I’ll use the `Column` component to structure the content within the tabs and the modal. Inside the `Tabs` component, I will define the tabs using an array of objects. Each object will define a tab, with a `title` and a nested child component (usually a `Column` itself).

The modal trigger is a button, which is a nested `Button` component inside the `Modal`. The content of the modal is another nested `Column` containing a confirmation message and buttons.

The data model will be initialized with `$/profile/name` for the name and `$/notifications/emailEnabled` for the notification setting. I will use the `(data ...)` structure to initialize these at the root level.
I also have to set the properties of `Text`, `Button`, `TextField`, `CheckBox`, etc. to the catalog parameters!

The final structure is as follows:
A `Column` (root) containing a `data` block, a title `Text`, the nested `Tabs` component, a `Divider`, and a `Modal` component (which itself contains a nested `Button` trigger and nested `Column` content). The `Tabs` will also nest `Column` components for each tab. Every component is nested.

I must include an `id` attribute on the root component because the prompt says to, and I will put `:id "root"` on the root `Column` component. I am not inventing any CSS or style attributes!

My final output will be a fully nested S-expression, adhering to all the specified rules and formatting requirements.

(Column :id "root"
  (data $/profile/name "Jane Doe" $/notifications/emailEnabled true)
  
  (Text :text "User Settings" :variant "body")
  
  (Tabs :tabs [
    {
      "title": "Profile",
      "child": (Column
                 (TextField :label "Name" :value $/profile/name :placeholder "Enter your name" :variant "shortText"))
    },
    {
      "title": "# Notifications",
      "child": (Column
                 (CheckBox :label "Enable email notifications" :value $/notifications/emailEnabled))
    }
  ])
  
  (Divider :axis "horizontal")
  
  (Modal
    :trigger (Button :child (Text :text "Delete Account") :action (Event "open_modal"))
    :content (Column
               (Text :text "Are you sure you want to delete your account? This action cannot be undone." :variant "body")
               (Row
                 (Button :child (Text :text "Confirm Deletion") :variant "primary" :action (Event "confirm_deletion"))
                 (Button :child (Text :text "Cancel") :variant "default" :action (Event "close_modal")))))
)
</a2ui>

Here's where things get interesting, because I have to pay special attention to the output format, especially nesting. I must use a nested tree structure. Component IDs cannot be declared separately. ## Instructions:
# A2UI Atom Output Contract

You must output the user interface using the compact A2UI Atom S-Expression notation.
You MUST surround the entire A2UI Atom block with the sentinel tags `<a2ui>` and `</a2ui>`.

IMPORTANT: Wrap your output inside `<a2ui>` and `</a2ui>` sentinel tags. Do NOT output raw JSON messages.

## Grammar Rules

1. Every component node is a parenthesized expression starting with the ComponentName:
   (ComponentName :key1 val1 :key2 val2 child1 child2 ...)

2. Primitives:
   - Strings: Double-quoted, e.g., "Hello". Escapes: \n, \t, \\, \".
   - Numbers: Integers or decimals, e.g., 42 or 3.14.
   - Booleans: true or false.
   - Null: null.

3. Property Arguments:
   - Tagged attributes: Prefixed with a colon ':', e.g., :attr1 "val1" or :attr2 true. Tagged keys are order-independent.
   - Positional attributes: Can be passed sequentially matching catalog signature order.

4. Child Components & Strict Tree Nesting:
   - You MUST nest child components directly inside their parent container expressions, e.g., (ContainerComponent (ChildComponent (PrimitiveComponent "Hello"))).
   - Do NOT output flat adjacency lists, explicit `:id` attributes, or separate component variable IDs. Every UI component must be nested directly within a single root tree expression.

5. Data Bindings:
   - Absolute data model paths start with '$/', e.g., $/user/firstName.
   - Relative template item fields start with '$/item_var/field', e.g. $/item/name.

6. Data Model Population:
   - Initialize or populate data model state exclusively using the (data $/path1 "val1" $/path2 123) block at the root level.

7. Dynamic List Templates:
   - List templates use (template :item item (ChildComponent $/item/name)) or (ListComponent :children (template :item item (ChildComponent $/item/name))).

8. Action Events:
   - Actions use (Event "action_name" :param1 $/value).

9. Standalone Operations:
   - Delete surface: (deleteSurface "surface_id")
   - Call RPC function: (callFunction "function_name" :arg1 "value1")

10. Syntax Structure Examples (Abstract Grammar):
   Example 1 (Container with Child Nodes & Actions):
   <a2ui>
   (ContainerComponent
     (ChildComponent :title "Header")
     (InputComponent :label "Input" :value $/form/field)
     (ActionComponent :label "Submit" :onPress (Event "submit_action" :val $/form/field)))
   </a2ui>

   Example 2 (Root Data State & Dynamic Template):
   <a2ui>
   (ContainerComponent
     (data $/items [{"id": 1, "name": "Item 1"}] $/title "List Title")
     (ListComponent :items $/items :template (template item (ChildComponent :title $/item/name))))
   </a2ui>

11. Strict Catalog Adherence:
   - You MUST ONLY use property names listed in the Component Catalog Signatures below.
   - Do NOT invent CSS or style attributes (e.g. style, padding, margin, backgroundColor, color, fontSize, size, minHeight, borderRadius, spacing, align, justify).

1. Construct the user interface on surfaceId 'main'.
2. If components are defined, ensure there is one root component with id: 'root'.

'borderless' means the button has no visual border or background, making its child content appear like a clickable link. Must be one of: 'default', 'primary', 'borderless'
  - :weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.
